pr_title: AI GroundAMState: complex terrain pathfinding fix
pr_body:
Fix #17327

1. Squad units will not all directly AttackMove to target, instead they regroup to a certain actor which will keep AttackMove pathfinding until death, which can greatly increase the AI pathfinding performance and much less stucked in complex maps.

2. Add a stucked check when pathfinding unit is stucked by friendly units/terrain/regroup. Make sure they can always approach the target when there is a route.

History:
> Thanks for @tovl advice on regrouping section.
> 
> I also add a stucked check when even the regrouping fix is not enough.
> 
> For performance, I add something to prevent giving out AttackMove order when unecessary.

Maps include TS elevated bridge can be much slower on AI ground squad moving compared to other maps, even in this fix. Units tend to pathfind to position that below bridge, so if leader at bridge units will try go below bridge even if they need to go back for that, and stuck check will be inevitable.

Other things may be questionable: 

1. `GetRandomValuableTarget` may be performance questionable. I want any ground squad switch target to shortgame-required target so they won't be confused by aircraft or other fast move target when choosing a main direction on advance. The key is whether the `manager.World.ActorsHavingTrait` is a highly cost method, even if used only once for a tick, at worst case.

2. Drop `ShouldFlee(owner)` in this function for better performance during my simplifying. Even if they need to escape, they can switch to ground state for that (also a `ShouldFlee(owner)` there). Strongly suggest take a look on `GroundAttackState` PR.

As far as your concerns about performance, I wouldn't be too concerned for now. I think that overall, this PR will actually improve performance greatly! 

Previously, all squad-members would pathfind towards the target individually at the same which would lead to noticeable lag spikes. In your current implementation, only the `pathGuide` will call the pathfinder for a path towards the target. The others will only ever try to path towards the `pathGuide` which are very short paths. Because of the way the A* algorithm scales, short paths are very cheap, but long paths are very expensive. I would expect this to be much more impactful than anything `GetRandomValuableTarget` does.

My totally not scientific anecdotic testing seems to confirm this. I got significant lag spikes, running a 6 AI player game on "A River Runs Near It" at fastest speed on bleed, but not with this PR. Perhaps @teinarss could confirm this in a bit more scientific way?

One funny edge case I noticed in my latest test: A squad containing several medics crosses a tiberium field. The medics are all trailing at the back because they are the slowest unit. The medics get stuck in a loop healing each other from the tiberium damage, while the squad leader waits patiently at the edge of the tiberium field :smile:

Update: Guess RV also have this issue (but I am not tested with Ai here with guard application). reason below.
What exactly is the problem stopping those mods from adding the `Guardable` trait to combat actors?

> What exactly is the problem stopping those mods from adding the Guardable trait to combat actors

1. Designer themselves don't consider that much and there is no AI module use Guard order. 

2. The bug in `TryRushAttack` in `SquadManager`. This function pick squad member by using:

```
			// TODO: This should use common names & ExcludeFromSquads instead of hardcoding TraitInfo checks
			var ownUnits = activeUnits
				.Where(unit => unit.IsIdle && unit.Info.HasTraitInfo<AttackBaseInfo>()
					&& !unit.Info.HasTraitInfo<AircraftInfo>() && !Info.NavalUnitsTypes.Contains(unit.Info.Name) && !unit.Info.HasTraitInfo<HarvesterInfo>()).ToList();
```

So this hardcoded line will pick all ground actor with attack base and ignore if this actor is just dummy actor for effect or non-combat units registration in `ExcludeFromSquads`. And then, crash.

@pchote 

Can we have a pure following (without attack) order used by AI? Hit and run AI will need that.

As for Guard vs AttackMove here in the face of functional, Guard is not always good. If we use Guard order which is equal to every units is in `unitsHurryUp` every tick. That will cause a problem: if guide is too slow, it will always be stuck by the squad members. 

Although stuck check and make way here can let the squad process to enemy but it will be much slower. There is no obvious benefits when we use guard order. 

You may say we can add a filter for the selection of the guide then we can use guard smoothly, I may agree but I think it will be a big work including speed, locomotor and actor filter and logic on choosing. I really don't want to add it now since squad manager is going to be refactored, and testing cost too much time and I wait long enough to get this merged. 

Add:
To solve "when guide is too slow, it will always be stuck by the squad members", I introduced `unitsHurryUp`, otherwise I can just let them attackmove

issue_context.title: Civilians wander onto Tiberium and spawn Visceroids
issue_context.body:
This random event can give an advantage to one player, or just end the game if it occurs in the first few minutes.

A possible solution is to have civilians avoid Tiberium, as suggested here: #18421
comments: We could bodge a workaround, but really the whole `Wanders` code needs a rewrite. My understanding is that this was a nice-to-have rather than a critical issue, so bumping to Next + 1.

review_comments:
These definitions don't make sense. The variable name suggests it is an area, but the value shows it is a distance, and it is used as if it were a squared distance.  The comments above ("we need to draw a circle to cover the the enitire circle.") doesn't help to clarify the intent.

I can see the general idea here, but I can't suggest specific name/comment changes to make the code more understandable until the logic is fixed to consistently use distance or squared distance or area.
